common_name: Fire Light Fab Hydrangea (Larger-Flowered Improved Fire Light Panicle Hydrangea)

planting.note: Plant container shrubs in spring or fall in moist, well-drained soil in full sun to partial shade; Fire Light Fab is an improved sport of Fire Light bred for even larger flower panicles and stronger stems.

directions: Plant in moist, well-drained, moderately fertile soil in full sun to partial shade. Fire Light Fab improves on the original Fire Light with even larger, denser flower panicles held on the same exceptionally sturdy, upright stems, opening white in summer and aging to a deep red-pink by late summer and fall. Like other panicle hydrangeas it blooms reliably on new wood, so a hard renewal pruning in late winter does not sacrifice the season's flowers. It tolerates more sun and less consistent moisture than mophead hydrangeas once established, and the strong stems keep the larger flower heads from flopping even after heavy rain, a common problem with older large-flowered panicle cultivars.

common_name: Little Lime Fab Hydrangea (Larger-Flowered Improved Little Lime Panicle Hydrangea)

planting.note: Plant container shrubs in spring in moist, well-drained, slightly acidic to neutral, moderately fertile soil in full sun to partial shade; Little Lime Fab is an improved sport of Little Lime with larger flower panicles on the same compact plant size.

directions: Plant in moist, well-drained, slightly acidic to neutral, moderately fertile soil in full sun to partial shade. Little Lime Fab keeps the same compact 3-to-5-foot size as the original Little Lime but produces noticeably larger, fuller flower panicles, opening chartreuse-green in midsummer, maturing to creamy white, and shifting through pink to dusty rose as they age into fall. Like all Hydrangea paniculata cultivars it blooms on new wood and is pruned hard in late winter to encourage vigorous new growth and maximum flower production, making it reliable regardless of pruning timing. In zone 9, morning sun with afternoon shade gives the best balance of flower production and heat protection, and the compact size suits foundation plantings and smaller garden spaces well.

common_name: Puffer Fish Hydrangea (Rounded Ball-Shaped Panicle Hydrangea)

planting.note: Plant container shrubs in spring or fall in moist, well-drained soil in full sun to partial shade; Puffer Fish is notable for unusually rounded, ball-shaped flower heads rather than the typical cone-shaped panicle of the species.

directions: Plant in moist, well-drained, moderately fertile soil in full sun to partial shade. Puffer Fish stands out among panicle hydrangeas for its unusual, dense, rounded flower heads that puff outward into a globe shape rather than the classic elongated cone typical of the species, opening white and aging to soft pink as summer progresses into fall. It blooms reliably on new wood, so a hard renewal pruning in late winter does not sacrifice the season's flowers, and its sturdy stems hold the rounded flower heads upright without flopping. Its distinctive flower form makes it a conversation-piece specimen or an unusual addition to a mixed shrub border, and it tolerates more sun and less consistent moisture than mophead hydrangeas once established.
